decisions.location: Introduction fourth aim; Results1.5.2 and Discussion, with complete2005/2006primary components and chain independently checked
decisions.quote: Fourth, I examined the effect of distraction. Even though Olivers and Nieuwenhuis (2006) hypothesise that there is a link between participants’ mood and attentional overinvestment, there is no clear-cut evidence for this. The previously reported diminished AB effect for participants who listened to music, who ruminated, or who were presented with positive pictures (Olivers & Nieuwenhuis, 2005, 2006) could have been due to different factors. First, the diminished AB in “distracted” participants compared to control participants could be due merely to changes in participants’ mood and not to distraction per se. Second, it could be due merely to the distraction that was present in the experimental conditions, regardless of the extent to which the distraction could be considered as “fun”. Third, it could be due to an 3 interaction between mood and distraction: possibly, diversion has positive effects on attentional control when this distraction induces specific emotions (e.g. happiness), but not when it induces other emotions (e.g. anxiety). Whereas the ideal experiment to examine separate effects of mood and distraction would be to manipulate mood while controlling for distraction in one condition, and to manipulate distraction while controlling for mood in another condition, the design of Jefferies et al. does allow for exploring the hypothesis that distraction in itself (regardless of mood) diminishes the AB effect. I examine this by comparing the control condition (in which participants did not receive an MIP and did not listen to music during the experiment) with the experimental conditions (in which participants did receive an MIP and listened to music during the experiment), a comparison that Jefferies et al. did not make. 1. Method I used the same method as Jefferies et al., with the exception that the instructions were provided in Dutch, as I tested native Dutch speakers at Ghent University. Second, participants were seated in a regular comfortable chair instead of a reclining lounge chair. The protocol can be found on the Open Science Framework (OSF) website, https://osf.io/g67tv/ 1.1. Participants I aimed to obtain a sample of at least 180 participants to obtain 80% power to detect the crucial interaction between valence and arousal on the difference bet
decisions.reason: Complete2005primary establishes the actual music/free-association empirical reduction in attentional blink, not a mere theory. Newly recovered complete2006primary explicitly calls its added-load and unfocused-instruction results replications of that pattern and separates an affective route; it is not solely a positive-picture paper. Current fourth aim/Results1.5.2 explicitly re-tests the named overinvestment/distraction finding using its new MIP/music versus no-MIP/music contrast. Under the codebook empirical-chain rule, the closest positively established2006retest is selected once for this current comparison, not an additional2005ancestor pair. This is not report equivalence or an exclusion merely because tasks differ. Current combines music, rumination and mood and does not isolate mechanisms. Jefferies2008existing1144covers its distinct mood/valence comparison and did not make this pooled distraction-control comparison. Raw earlier2005positive and2006negative opinions remain unchanged; no outcome requested.

decisions.reason: New complete2006primary materially corrects the premise of the final raw negative: Experiment1empirically tests added cognitive load and Experiment3unfocused instructions, in addition to affective pictures, and explicitly presents these as re-tests of2005distraction benefits. Current identifies2006overinvestment, designs its fourth aim to examine distraction regardless of mood, and tests pooled new MIP/music observations against no-distraction controls in1.5.2. Thus it conceptually re-tests this published distraction/overinvestment finding; lack of the original line-memory task or pictures is not an exclusion. The same current contrast is counted at the closest verified2006empirical report rather than again at2005ancestor. Complete primary identities and new reported samples distinguish this chain from alternate reports; pooled original T1analyses are not counted as another cohort. Existing1144Jefferies2008addresses mood/valence and omitted the distraction-control comparison, so it does not represent this additional target. Keep source-printed citation title and empty DOI; no external identifier silently inserted. No outcome requested.
